report.summary: The change makes the Artifacts repo.log lookups in branchTips and artifactHeadSha pass the plain branch name instead of refs/heads/<branch>. That matches the binding's generated type contract (ref: 'Branch, tag, or commit ID'). The test fakes no longer remove a refs/heads/ prefix, so a regression would now fail, and one test asserts the exact calls. The forge-demo regexes now match both Node 24 test output styles (spec 'ℹ fail 0' and TAP '# fail 0') and keep word boundaries. Failure paths, ownership and read-only checks are unchanged, and no spec change is needed. Tests were not run because dependencies are not installed in this worktree; the review is based on reading the code. There are two non-blocking notes.

findings.text: Not blocking: the plain name is resolved by the binding as 'Branch, tag, or commit ID'. BRANCH_NAME does not reject 40-hex names or names that match a tag, so such a branch could resolve to a commit or a tag instead of the branch. This is rare. Confirming it needs the binding's precedence rules or a live check.

evidence.why: worker-runtime.d.ts documents ref as 'Branch, tag, or commit ID' and does not state which form wins when a name matches more than one.

findings.text: Not blocking: the fake now accepts only plain branch names, which matches the documented contract. Proof that the real binding fails to resolve refs/heads/<branch> (the original bug) comes only from the type docs and the commit's claim. A live e2e run (forge-demo) would confirm it.

evidence.why: A fake shows the code calls log with the plain name, not that the real binding resolves it.

checked.risk: Real contracts (Cloudflare Artifacts binding repo.log ref semantics)
Failure paths (empty log result still becomes NOT_FOUND or null, errors not swallowed)
Security (repo id and read-only checks still run before lookup, branch validation unchanged)
Build and runtime environment (Node 24 test reporter output format for forge-demo regexes)
Tests (fakes no longer accept both forms, exact call assertion, no sleeps added)
